title:
Environmental intelligence.
Shared across the field.
voice: Meet Gaia. A distributed environmental intelligence platform where sensor nodes interpret local conditions, cooperate with their neighbours, and share a view of the environment.

title:
Intelligence where
measurements happen.
voice: Environmental monitoring reaches farms, forests, buildings, and waterways. These places need useful local information, even when internet access is unreliable or unavailable.

title:
One foundation.
Many environmental profiles.
voice: Soil moisture could reveal irrigation needs. Carbon dioxide could guide ventilation. Water sensors could identify changing conditions. Each application needs its own sensors, model, and validation.

title:
Sense. Interpret.
Cooperate.
voice: Each node reads its sensors and computes local state. Nearby nodes exchange that state to build collective fields. A local network carries the messages, without requiring a cloud service.

title:
The thermal
reference demonstrator.
voice: Our current demonstrator uses three Arduino Uno Q boards and temperature and humidity sensing. The thermal scenario makes the underlying cooperation visible through physical lights and a dashboard.

title:
Learning the
local baseline.
voice: The current model learns normal temperature and watches its rate of rise. Humidity is displayed, but does not yet drive the score. Neighbours share model statistics every fifteen seconds.

title:
A local change.
A distributed field.
voice: Heat one node and it becomes a source. Its neighbours compute their distance from that source. A single abnormal node creates the gradient, while the consensus alert remains off.

title:
Neighbours
confirm the event.
voice: When an adjacent node also detects the anomaly, the two sources agree. The stronger consensus alert activates. This separates early local detection from collective confirmation.

title:
A changing network.
A field that adapts.
voice: Disconnect a node. After the timeout, neighbours recompute their state. A disconnected region may lose its known path. When the node returns, communication and the field recover.

title:
Close the dashboard.
The nodes continue.
voice: The dashboard observes the network. Close it, and the nodes continue sensing, exchanging state, and updating their lights. Local coordination runs on the boards themselves.

title:
A shared view
of the environment.
voice: The digital twin brings telemetry, topology, and environmental state together. Building and forest simulations also demonstrate route changes. These simulated routes are separate from physical node guidance.

title:
From field state
to clear language.
voice: A deterministic report describes the network state. An optional local Gemma model rewrites that report for people. It does not create measurements, decide alerts, or choose routes.

title:
Measured in
our reference demo.
voice: The included indoor recording contains three hundred and two normal samples and seventy heated samples. These results support the thermal demonstration, and require broader validation before real environmental deployment.

title:
The next profile
starts with the environment.
voice: The next step is a versioned profile system and a second application, such as carbon dioxide or soil moisture. Secure device identity and profile-specific datasets will support future field trials.

title:
Local understanding.
Collective environmental intelligence.
voice: Gaia brings sensing, local learning, and neighbour cooperation into one environmental platform. Today, the thermal demonstrator proves the approach. The wider vision spans agriculture, air, water, and ecosystems.
